_note: Single source of truth for meelTe visual identity. Skills and agents READ this file. Do not copy hex values into prompts or skill files; reference the token name instead so a palette change propagates everywhere.

brand.name: meelTe
name_rules: Never render 'MELTE', 'Meelte.', 'Meelte Inc', or a split wordmark unless the supplied logo asset shows it.
The brand name in copy is never abbreviated and never lowercased.
brand.positioning: The friendly technology partner for local businesses.
brand.promise: Make local business owners feel understood and empowered.
tone_rules: Speak to the owner, not about the software.
Lead with the business benefit; technology is the how, never the headline.
Warm and plain-spoken. No enterprise jargon, no growth-hacker language.
Confident, never boastful. No superlatives that cannot be substantiated.
Celebrate the local business owner as the hero; Meelte is the helpful tool.

orange.usage: Dominant accent. CTAs, highlight shapes, key numerals, energy. Use as the first colour the eye lands on.
orange.on_white: OK for large text and shapes; not for body copy under 18px.

purple.usage: Dominant brand anchor. Headlines, logo lockups, large shapes, trust surfaces.

lavender.usage: Breathing room, background panels, card fills, soft separation.
lavender.on_white: Never use for text. Background only.

charcoal.usage: Typography, outlines, high-contrast text, deep backgrounds.

white.usage: Clarity, negative space, text on purple or charcoal, card surfaces.

palette.dominance_note: Targets are a sanity check, not a pixel budget. Orange and purple together must read as the dominant pair in any creative.
rules: Orange + purple are the dominant brand pair. If a third hue is needed, it must be a campaign-specific reason documented in the brief.
Lavender and white carry negative space; charcoal carries text.
Never place orange text on purple or purple text on orange for anything smaller than a headline.
Never tint the palette (no pastel orange, no navy 'brand purple'). Use the exact hex values.
Keep one clear contrast hierarchy: charcoal or white text, one accent, one background.
Gradients are allowed only between two brand tokens and only as subtle depth, never as a rainbow.
banned_colors: teal / cyan as a dominant colour
black (#000000) as a substitute for charcoal

headline.case: Sentence case preferred; Title Case allowed

rules: Bold geometric sans only. No serif, no script, no condensed grotesque.
One type family per creative. Do not mix Poppins with Manrope in the same layout.
Never stretch, squash, outline, or add drop shadows to type.
Never use all-caps for anything longer than 3 words.
Never letterspace body copy.
Do not render small text in the image model; put it in a text-safe area and overlay deterministically.

logo.selection_rule: Pick the variant by background: full-colour on white/lavender, reverse-white on purple/charcoal, mono-charcoal only when colour reproduction is unavailable.
logo.clear_space: 0.5 x mark height on all four sides, minimum.

placement.default: footer band, left or right aligned
never: placed on a busy or low-contrast area
recreated, redrawn, or approximated from memory

logo.integrity_rule: If no approved logo file is supplied, leave a reserved logo zone and mark the deliverable 'logo pending'. Never fabricate, trace, or generate the Meelte logo.

illustration.style_name: Playful Modern Branding + Flat Vector Illustration + Bold Editorial Advertising

attributes.shapes: flat vector forms with subtle gradients for depth
attributes.characters: friendly, expressive faces, rounded slightly exaggerated proportions
attributes.detail: controlled; one focal point, uncluttered background
attributes.palette: limited and intentional, drawn from the brand tokens

banned_treatments: unrelated illustration styles (anime, gritty sketch, low-poly, watercolour, memphis revival)
illustration.override_rule: A different style is permitted only when the user explicitly requests it, and the override must be recorded in the campaign brief.

rules: People must be contextually appropriate to the market and campaign audience.
Avoid stereotypes of profession, gender, age, or region.
Props must earn their place; no filler objects to balance the frame.
Smartphone props communicate Meelte's digital capability only when relevant.

principles: One central illustration or focal subject.
One call to action, only when required.
Consistent logo placement and adequate safe margins.
The message must be understandable in under three seconds.
rules: Never force a 1:1 layout onto another ratio; recompose per format.
Never let two elements compete for the same focal weight.
Never crowd the frame; negative space is part of the design.
Text must never sit on a busy illustration area without a solid or scrim panel.

copy.claim_policy: Never invent prices, offers, discounts, statistics, product capabilities, or customer claims. If a fact is not in the brief, it does not appear in the creative.
copy.text_rendering_note: Project default is in_image: the generation host is a text-capable model (Nano Banana Pro, Ideogram), so the headline is rendered and QA'd character by character. Switch to overlay_after_generation when the model is unreliable at text or when a deterministic overlay layer is available. Either way, a price, date, or legal line may appear only if the user supplied the exact string.
